gate.judge: overall >= 4, distinctiveness >= 4, and no individual dimension below 4
gate.user: explicit approval of each timed target animatic and the capability-gap memo

defects.note: Console and checklist read as co-equal focal elements; the paired layout is intentional (code beside checks) but slightly divides attention at the resolution beat.
Motion is limited to reveals, a subtle checklist scale, and the loop fade; no true push/pan/focus move to actively guide the eye.

judge.notes: A specific, well-branded release-gate loop that resolves cleanly and restarts seamlessly; its only real ceiling is modest camera work and the dual-focal build shot, keeping it a solid pass rather than exceptional.

The board shot packs a full dashboard (three stats, four service rows, and a drawing latency chart with small mono labels) into ~4.8s, so at social-film downscale it leans dense and is the weakest link for readability; everything else, especially the amber-spike to green-recovery queue-latency motif that recurs across hook, board, resolve, and payoff, is specific and coherent enough to survive a product-name swap.

defects.note: Transitions between shots are hard cuts (enter/exit 0); the only true camera move is a subtle 6px push + 1.2% scale on the tour-grid during explain, so causality reads mainly from the copy/rule-highlight swaps rather than motion.
The palette and the explain/step panel share the frame; the lit rule row does guide the eye, but two competing panels slightly soften the single-focal-point read.

judge.notes: Strong, product-specific tour: real fuzzymatch objects (src/index.js subsequence highlights, +0.42/+0.21/-0.12 scoring rules, 3.7ms/10k-files/~2KB money shot) and a coherent violet identity, with clean hook and payoff and no empty-frame or text collisions. Weakest link is camera personality: it leans on hard cuts and text swaps with only a whisper of a push, so distinctiveness comes from the motif rather than the motion.
